'''Tandia''' is a recently extinct [[Austronesian language]]. Most speakers have shifted to [[Wandamen language|Wandamen]]. In 1991, there were worldwide only two speakers of Tandia, both of whom lived just south of the Wohsimi River on the [[Wandamen Peninsula]], [[Irian Jaya]] Province, [[Indonesia]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Did you know Tandia is critically endangered? |url=http://www.endangeredlanguages.com/lang/2789 |website=endangeredlanguages.com}}</ref> It was confirmed to be a living language in 2009, but, by 2024, it was found to have gone extinct by a linguistic survey team.<ref>{{Cite web |date=8 March 2024 |title=11 Indigenous Languages Declared Extinct: Education Ministry |url=https://jakartaglobe.id/news/11-indigenous-languages-declared-extinct-education-ministr |access-date=10 September 2024 |website=Jakarta Globe}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=((Desk)) |first=((News)) |title=Four Papuan languages extinct, linguist says - Archipelago |url=https://www.thejakartapost.com/indonesia/2024/02/22/four-papuan-languages-extinct-linguist-says.html |access-date=2026-04-08 |website=The Jakarta Post |language=en}}</ref>

It was a primary branch of the [[South Halmahera–West New Guinea languages]].
